subject: chemistry

moments.title: Schönbein notices a smell
moments.body: Schönbein, electrolysing water, notices a sharp smell — and names it 'ozone' from the Greek for 'to smell'. He shows it is a strong oxidant. The molecular structure remains unclear for decades.
moments.takeaway: A new oxidant is identified by its smell.

moments.title: Soret shows O3
moments.body: Soret demonstrates that ozone is triatomic oxygen (O3). It is allotropic — same element, different molecular form.

moments.title: Stratospheric ozone layer
moments.body: Fabry and Buisson show much of the Sun's UV is absorbed by an ozone layer at 15-35 km altitude. The layer protects all surface life from harmful UV-B and UV-C.
moments.takeaway: Life on land is enabled by atmospheric ozone.

moments.title: Ozone hole confirmed
moments.body: Antarctic stratospheric ozone has dropped 40% — confirming Molina-Rowland predictions about CFCs. Montreal Protocol follows in 1987.
moments.takeaway: Industrial chemicals nearly destroyed the planetary UV shield.

now.title: Where we are today
now.body: Stratospheric ozone is slowly recovering. Tropospheric (ground-level) ozone, however, is rising in many cities and damaging crops and lungs.
now.open_questions: How will climate-driven changes to stratospheric dynamics affect ozone recovery?

reflection: Schönbein smelled ozone in 1839 without knowing what it was. How often do we sense phenomena before naming them?
